best_for: Windows users who must stay on the old open-source Community Edition, for a locked-down machine or a course that names it, and need a specific build.

points.title: This line has ended
points.text: JetBrains says 2025.2 was the last major release of PyCharm Community Edition. The newest build listed here is 2025.2.6.1, and no new feature releases will follow.

points.title: The free path is unified PyCharm
points.text: From 2025.3, Community users are moved to the single PyCharm product. Its core features stay free and add Jupyter notebook support, with a one-click Pro trial on top.

points.title: Open source, Apache-2.0
points.text: Community Edition is licensed Apache-2.0. JetBrains says the open-source parts stay public on GitHub, and you can still build them from source with GitHub Actions.

points.title: Pin an exact build
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 69 versions, which helps if a course, plugin or company image needs one exact release.

points.title: Windows only here
points.text: This site lists Community Edition for Windows only, in x64 and Arm64 builds that install per user or for the whole machine. Mac and Linux users should look at unified PyCharm instead.
